Friends,
Zahid doesn't want to tell me how he's doing. He knows how to put on a smile through pain - he's been doing it since his injuries. (The ones the doctors thought would drive him to suicide, twenty years ago.)
But after awhile, proximity to pain gives you an intuition. You start to be able to read the cloudiness of the eyes, the slight lowering of the brows, and you can tell - this man is suffering. Chronic migraines and traumatic brain injury do not combine well with 24/7 exposure to fluorescent light.
_(yes - even during the 12am-5am "sleep" cycles, the lights are just dimmed by half. Never, ever off.)_
And so, those of us who know him well enough, we sit down across the glass and listen while he talks to us over the phone, and we read the subtle cues - the pain lines, the shadowed brow, the subjects he never touches on.
He's in excruciating pain. Constantly. And there's nothing we can do about it.
Try, please, to imagine the dehumanizing confinement: no darkness for resting, ever - and no windows. No sunlight and no sky. No soil, no view of a tree, not even the ability to tell if it's raining. _No windows_.
It's important for you to understand - **rapists and murderers are treated better than this.** We have _standards_ for "prisoners." Legal requirements. Windows, recreation, true exercise and time outside, the ability to hug their families during visits.
**There are no legal standards for ICE detention centers.**
Sure, there's "policy." "Guidelines." But no actual _rules_.
Despite years upon years, now, of [cleanliness and health concerns](https://substack.com/redirect/5fb44793-441f-4d7e-97b5-612d1e1d2876?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) \- including from ICE and GEO employees _fearful of their safety at work_ \- enforcing any standards or ensuring any improvement would require ICE giving a damn about the people they throw away.
I'm not holding my breath.
In fact I'm blowing it out, slowly, as I often do these days. Earlier, before I could bring myself to write to you, the tears were falling without my noticing, again. That happened three times today.
* * *
People ask me how Zahid's doing. In the worst possible moments, when they should know better - for instance, at the start of a nice meal with friends, the first in weeks.
First, ok, now I'm feeling guilty about the nice meal in front of me and the presence of friends, knowing full well that Zahid has neither, hasn't for many weeks, and won't for, probably, many more.
Knowing that Zahid's breakfast is a spoonful of mashed potatoes, a couple of tablespoons of cornflakes, _maybe_ a half-pint of milk (and he had to fight for a full month to get the milk). Fresh fruit? Couple times a week, maybe. Maybe.
Then, ok, sure, you want me to go into that now? How he's doing? Thought exercise, go with me on this please - _how would you be doing?_
Imagine you're suddenly and arbitrarily cut off from family and friends, locked in a concrete box with no sunlight and no fresh air, underfed, overpoliced, crowded with dozens of strangers, under the control of guards who disdain you, with _constant_ violent TV noise, with no exercise, with no peace and quiet, with no solitude, with no affection, with never a full meal, with certain knowledge of your innocence (except there are no charges against you), and with no end in sight.
Now imagine you're disabled - in a wheelchair, with a broken back and neck that immobilize you with pain for hours. Imagine the relentless migraines throbbing, the acid burning you from the inside out day and night. Imagine you're denied your pain medication. Your eye medicine to keep from going blind. The simple relief of baking soda to drink with water. Let alone... your spouse. Your children.
Denied all that stabilized and comforted you. (Never mind any possibility of solace or purpose or delight.)
Imagine that _you had done nothing wrong_. Imagine that _the country you love and served, body and blood and soul, and gave the best years of your life to, had turned around and done this to you in return._
Friends, I ask you...
_**What on God 's green earth do you want me to say??!**_
It's Not Good, y'all!
It's terrible!
It's inhumane, and it's horrific, and it's dehumanizing, and it's maddening, and it's senseless, and it's painful, and it's cruel!
_And people are making money from this!_
And all that hasn't changed since the last time you asked, no really it hasn't. I promise you I'd shout the good news from the rooftops if it had.
It's only gotten worse.
Sure. Yes. He smiles, which means nothing. He tells us to stay strong... \- sure he does. (He did, anyway, the first week.)
Now all he wants to talk about is sunlight. Rain. Childhood memories. Cooking meat. The taste of my daal (spiced lentils). He tells me over and over now, how good my daal is. Was. Will be.
(Insha'Allah.)
There's no improvement, there's only suffering, and you would do all of us a favor if you'd just acknowledge, now, that you know that, and not ask me to tell you how he's doing, because the blinding helpless grieving rage you throw me back into, inside, knowing that the soul of my soul and solace of my life is caged worse than neglected animals, knowing that the most beautiful and brilliant human I've ever been so deeply blessed to know is being treated like worse than nothing, day and night and day again...
_c 'mon. please. i'm trying to stay functional, here._
* * *
If you want the raw truth of it, I don't know how he's staying sane.
... Or me, for that matter. Me, either.
Except that I have everything he doesn't - the kids, the sun, food, family, rest, peace, freedom.
Through no special right of my own. Nothing I did right that he did wrong. He did nothing to deserve this. No one does.
The arbitrariness of it. The inhumanity of it.
Of course, it's designed to break us. That doesn't mean it will.
But it does mean I need you to understand something very clearly,
_**The cruelty is the point**_.
* * *
In other news, we got his bond appeal in a couple of days ago.
Making the argument to the Board of Immigration Appeals that he shouldn't be in there. (Obviously.) That the judge erred in finding "no jurisdiction." (Duh.) And that because she's already got a class action lawsuit against her about this, and she spent her career as a lawyer for ICE, they shouldn't remand (send) the case back down for her to reconsider, they should just decide the custody matter themselves.
_Did you know the incredible importance of the difference between INA § 236 (a) and INA §1231 ?_ I didn't. Turns out it's the difference between letting him go in peace and freedom, and ... everything I described to you above.
In terms of legal steps, those are the big ones. After the flurry of 9th Circuit filings last week, and the Bond Appeal this week, now it's mostly a waiting game.
* * *
Which means, it's time to get busy. Time to share human stories at scale. Time to reclaim the algorithmic battlefield AND create real, meaningful, in-person connections. We need to beat the masters of narrative at their own game, and the best way to do that is steadily, consistently, calmly, humanizing everyone they attack and disdain.
This article gives [great instructions on the how](https://open.substack.com/pub/antwest12/p/congratulations-youve-been-flagged). And if you're one of those people who shuns social media because of the toxicity, I feel you, but here's [why we need to fight back](https://open.substack.com/pub/lukium/p/stop-bringing-a-picket-sign-to-a-psyop-fight) (and how to do it without losing your mind).
I'll still be here, still loving our kids, still tending the garden, still organizing for justice. Still visiting him, letting him talk to me and see my face and hear my voice, hear stories from outside, be listened to, be heard.
I hope you will be, too.
* * *
What is happening to Zahid is not an abstraction. It's not a policy debate or a headline. It's a father who aches for sunlight, a husband who remembers the taste of daal, two little children who wonder where Baba is. It's also a system that feeds on human suffering--_and counts on our silence to keep it alive._
But we are not silent. Every visit, every filing, every post, every act of witness **chips away at the walls built to disappear him and others like him**. We are fighting to bring him home, and to end this cruelty for everyone.
So if you're reading this, please: don't look away. Share Zahid's story. Tell your friends, your networks, your elected officials. Help us hold the line for him--and for the thousands whose names you may never know.
Together, we can make sure the cruelty is not the last word.
For the kids' sake - ours, yours, and everyone's.

This election isn’t weeks away, t’s happening right now. | | | Friend — This election isn’t weeks away. It’s happening **_right now_**. As of today, at least**1,687****votes have already been cast in our district**. That number is climbing every day. And between now and Election Day on November 4 — it is our job to get as many people to vote as possible. That means every dollar we raise today goes straight into reaching voters who are already making up their minds. Every canvass shift, every call, every piece of literature at the door — **_matters now_** _**more**_** _than ever._** Now, let’s be clear: our opponents know this too. They’re already spending **big** to bank early votes, because they know every ballot cast now is one less to fight for on Election Day.******If we let them run up the score, it’ll be too late to catch up.** **We can’t afford that.** _Not in a district Kamala Harris carried by less than 1%. subject: Here’s how you can help Democrats take back the Senate majority:

body:
We don’t want to show any weakness.
| | [Our campaign’s first FEC end-of-quarter filing deadline is just days away. Split a donation of any size between our team and the Voter Protection Project to help meet our goal before time runs out »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/94235?t=6&akid=21332%2E878179%2EiJEuPz)

Hello friend,

I’m reaching out about our upcoming filing deadline — the first of our campaign so far — but I wanted to make sure you had some important context:

**Nationwide, Republicans and GOP-aligned groups have been outraising Democrats in the lead-up to next year’s midterm elections, and our election in North Carolina is expected to become the most expensive U.S. Senate race in history.**

My GOP opponent and his allies will be forced to make spending decisions they may not want to make based on what we can raise now, friend. With all that in mind, it’s even more important for us to show our financial strength in this report.

This is the most consequential Senate election of 2026, and if we win here, Democrats have the chance to take back the majority and stop the far-right’s extreme agenda. Meeting our fundraising goals is key to our chances of success in this toss-up race.

But we have a long way to go to hit our end-of-quarter target, and we’re running out of time to get there.

[We can’t risk allowing my GOP opponent to outraise us, so I need your help right away. Does a contribution, split between our campaign and the Voter Protection Project, fit in your budget today? »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/94235?t=7&akid=21332%2E878179%2EiJEuPz)

I am running for Congress because, for too long (13 years!), Congressman Scott Perry has failed to step up to the plate and address the very real concerns of our friends and neighbors. Instead, he cut healthcare access for seniors and our disabled neighbors, backed tariffs that make things more expensive, and voted to give tax breaks to multi-millionaires. = If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will process now. | = | = | = | = | = | = At the end of the day, this campaign is about people. subject: No one should receive a medal for murdering innocent men, women and children
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO
body:
Time and again, our government has chosen cruelty over justice when it comes to Native people.
# [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/133?t=1&akid=4678%2E400544%2EdbjqTR)
This is shameful.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/804?t=2&akid=4678%2E400544%2EdbjqTR)
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth is reaffirming the medals of those who carried out the massacre at Wounded Knee. **That wasn’t a battle — it was the murder of hundreds of Lakota people, mostly women and children.** The government is now claiming that violence deserves honor.
I come from a military family. My father was a Marine, my mother served in the Navy, and I carry their spirit of service in my own life. Military members like my father honorably earn their medals by exhibiting incredible courage against foreign enemies during wartime. **No one should receive a medal for murdering innocent women and children.**
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250926_2_rr?amount=5&refcode=em20250926-4678&refcode2=4678_400544_dbjqTR&akid=4678%2E400544%2EdbjqTR)_My father was a U.S. Marine Corps combat veteran. My mother served in the Navy._
Standing at the gravesite with descendants of those victims brought home to me how the trauma of that day still lingers in the community. **And time and again, our government has chosen cruelty over justice when it comes to Native people.**
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250926_2_rr?amount=5&refcode=em20250926-4678&refcode2=4678_400544_dbjqTR&akid=4678%2E400544%2EdbjqTR)_As Secretary of the Interior, I was honored to join with community members who live with the trauma of that tragedy and pay respect to those who were unjustly killed at Wounded Knee. _
New Mexico — home to military service members and veterans — deserves a governor who will face the truth of our history and will fight to ensure _every_ community across the state is respected and has the opportunity to thrive.
**[This campaign _must_ win — not just for me, but for every community that has been told their lives matter less. Please, if you’re able, chip in $5 today to help us build the movement we need.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250926_2_rr?amount=5&refcode=em20250926-4678&refcode2=4678_400544_dbjqTR&akid=4678%2E400544%2EdbjqTR)**

In solidarity,
Deb Haaland
